). The `{projectId}` segment accepts the literal `default` for the key org's Default project. Most users never call these directly
— set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` and the [SDK reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/concepts/saving-results.md) does:\n\n| Endpoint | What

it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-ingest/report` | One-shot: create a run from finished results and finalize it |
| `POST ..
./eval-ingest/runs/start` | Chunked flow: create (or idempotently reuse) a run by `externalRunId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/
iterations` | Append an iteration batch to a started run |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/finalize` | Finalize a chunked run (idemp
otent) |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` | Store one artifact's raw bytes (widget HTML too large to send inline) and return it
s `storageId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts/upload-url` | Retired. Answers `410 Gone` with `details.code: \"SDK_UPGRADE_REQ
UIRED\"`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload artifacts with `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` instead |\n\n**Agent** (`/projects
/{projectId}/agent`) — a headless assistant turn for\nbuilding conversational surfaces (the MCPJam Slack app is the first consumer

):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../agent` | Run ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: "use
r\"\\|\"assistant\", content}` items, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 96 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to the
project. The turn can read project servers/suites/runs and **create eval suites**; it can NOT start runs — kick those off yoursel
f with `POST .../eval-runs`. Responds synchronously with `reply`, the `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links), a
nd token `usage`. Capped at 4 concurrent turns per organization and \\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent — never blind-retry**: de
dupe on your own trigger identity, and on an error response check `details.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list sui

tes) before retrying, or you'll create duplicates |

**Studies** (`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it d

oes |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies` | List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |
|
`GET .../studies/{studyId}` | One study's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environmen
t it publishes, and its insights envelope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, nev

er null |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Swarms and User Testing are enabled per organization.** Everything in the
> four sections below is
behind that gate, enforced server-side. If it is not\n> on for your organization, the reads generally return empty and every **wr
ite**\n> — creating a persona or goal, launching a run, publishing a study,\n> requesting insights — answers `403` with a message

naming the feature, not a
> `404` and not a validation error.
>
> Five operations are deliberately outside the gate, because ev
ery one of them\n> *reduces* exposure and spend: cancelling a goal run, unpublishing a\n> study, and archiving a persona, goal or
swarm (each one's `DELETE`). An\n> organization that loses access can still stop what is running and clean up\n> what it authored.

>
> Ask us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) if you want it turned on.

**Swarms — authoring** (`/projects/{project
Id}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,\n`.../swarms...`) — the definitions a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a\nreusable synthetic
character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is an authoring container holding defaults for the goals made\nu

nder it. Nothing here starts anything — launching is
`POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
|
`GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |\n| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GE
T .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so r
enaming is safe |\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still reference it |\n| `GET .../go
als` | List the project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must
be in this project |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `enviro
nmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing runs
keep pointing at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swa
rm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update th
e container's defaults. Not a cascade — existing goals keep their own values |\n| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **Archive** a sw

arm. The goals under it stay launchable |

**Swarms — generation** — drafts a model writes for you. Both routes return
candidat
es and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create\nroutes above. That is also why neither accepts an `Idempoten
cy-Key` — a call\nwith no effect has nothing to de-duplicate, and offering one would imply the\ndrafts are stable across retries w

hen they are not.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../personas/generate` | Draft a slate of personas (and goals
for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment |\n| `POST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals for a persona passed **b

y value**, so you can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
>
> The generation routes consume **no customer credits** — the mo
del cost is on\n> MCPJam. They are still subject to usage limits, and each limit means a\n> different wait: a per-minute burst bra
ke (`429`, retry in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generation quota (`429`, resets at UTC midnight), and\n> MCPJam's own d
aily budget for the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform_capacity\"`, resets at UTC midnight). All three carry\n> `Ret
ry-After` — honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `false`\n> on every one: buying credits does not lift them, so do

not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

**Swarms — runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/runs`

,
`.../goal-runs/...`) — launching a goal and reading what it produced:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goa
ls/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |\n| `POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.** Answers `202` — the fan-out h
as started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSponsored` is how many conversations you expect MCPJam to spon
sor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_changed`) and nothing is created. The response can report `
funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}` | The full run: counts, per-target breakdown, per-sess
ion `attempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sessions the run produced (summaries, not transcripts) |\n| `P
OST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent — a second cancel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409` |\

n
Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model cre
dits, so a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Replaying a key\n returns the original run with `deduped:
true` and starts no second runner —\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the header is read as a request that declined\n to identif
y itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before reporting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \
"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a status of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the
runner went silent\n and the watchdog settled the run.\n* **`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can

resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two
 targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
>
Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`\n> sessions. Two different `429`s can come back — the per-minute
burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC midnight).\n> Both normally carry `Retry-After`
